item.title: China urges G7 to 'put its own house in order' as G7 foreign ministers hype Taiwan question in statement
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12 19:30:00
The logo of G7 Photo: VCG G7 foreign ministers, in a joint declaration issued late on Wednesday, once again hyped up China's activities in the waters east of Taiwan island, claiming the activities threaten regional stability and freedom of navigation. The move later prompted a response from the Chinese side, which said on Thursday that the statement disregarded objective facts and urged the G7 to "put its own house in order and fulfill its responsibilities." The declaration, issued following their meeting in Paris on November 9-10, also expressed so-called support for Taiwan's "meaningful participation in international organizations." China had taken note of the joint statement on the Taiwan question issued following the G7 Foreign Ministers' Meeting, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Thursday, noting that China's position on the Taiwan question has always been clear, consistent, justified and aboveboard. The statement disregards objective facts and China's positive contributions to world peace, stability and development, grossly interferes in China's internal affairs, and maliciously smears and vilifies China. Mao said during the press conference that China urges the G7 to put its own house in order, fulfill its responsibilities, and play a more constructive role in addressing today's pressing challenges and promoting international solidarity. A Reuters report said on Thursday that while the US, Britain, France and Germany have all previously expressed their concern about China's actions off Taiwan's east coast, the G7 statement is the "strongest unified expression of concern to date about the Chinese activities." The spokesperson previously responded to a question regarding China's maritime activities off Taiwan island's east coast in October, saying that China has an exclusive economic zone and continental shelf in waters east of the Taiwan island. It is fully within China's sovereign rights and jurisdiction, therefore legitimate, lawful and beyond reproach, for China to carry out activities in these waters, Mao continued. "The party that instigates trouble and disrupts stability in this part of waters has never been the Chinese side," Mao also emphasized. The joint declaration of G7 foreign ministers also garnered coverage within the Taiwan region, with the island's Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities seizing on it to express "sincere welcome and appreciation" on Thursday, according to Taiwan's CNA. In recent years, G7 members have each played up the Taiwan question for different reasons, said Dong Yifan, an associate research fellow at the Academy of International and Regional Studies, Beijing Language and Culture University. Japan uses it to advance its militarization ambitions, while the US views it through the lens of strategic competition with China, Dong said. "Certain European countries, meanwhile, seek to use the Taiwan question to shape transatlantic relations, particularly as China has recently approached an important juncture in multilateral diplomacy." While each member has its own agenda, their purpose of hyping the Taiwan question is to create a common adversary, Dong added. By playing up regional security issues, they are laying the political groundwork for potential moves toward alliance-building and expansion in the economic and military spheres, the expert said.

item.title: Hong Kong bill to tighten teacher registration rules and prevent people convicted of national security offences from teaching
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12 19:09:00
Hong Kong file photo The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) government said on Thursday that it would gazette the Education (Amendment) Bill 2026 on Friday, with the aim of enhancing the teacher registration mechanism by imposing practising certificate requirements, and introducing a mechanism to handle matters of teacher registration for persons convicted of offences endangering national security, according to a SAR government press release. The release noted that the move is to ensure that all teachers are fit and proper persons, thereby upholding the professionalism of the teaching force. The bill will establish statutory requirements for all teachers, including principals, of publicly-funded schools, private schools, international schools and kindergartens to possess teacher registration and practising certificates to serve in schools. The validity period of a practising certificate would be no more than three school years. The bill will also set out the requirements for applying for practising certificates, according to the release. There will be a mandatory continuing professional development requirement for teachers to obtain practising certificates, thus ensuring that all teachers keep abreast of the latest global and local educational policies, and that their knowledge and pedagogy align with students' and societal needs, to further enhance the professionalism of the teaching force, it said. The bill would also introduce safeguards to prevent persons convicted of offences endangering national security from teaching in schools to effectively protect students, uphold the professional integrity of teachers and maintain public confidence in the teaching profession. A spokesman for the Education Bureau (EDB) said the bill meets schools' actual operational needs, encourages teachers to keep pace with the times and strengthens teacher management, with the ultimate goal of safeguarding the well-being of students. The EDB has consulted the sector since September 2025 and the Legislative Council (LegCo) Panel on Education on February 6 this year. The Bill will be introduced in LegCo for First Reading and Second Reading on November 25. Global Times

item.title: NASA renews Mars sample-return push as US media cites China pressure; experts warn rivalry narrative could backfire
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12 17:01:00
China's Tianwen-3 mission is scheduled to launch around 2028 Schematic diagram: VCG As NASA renews its push to bring Martian samples back to Earth, US media has cited progress in China's Tianwen-3 mission as a source of competitive pressure. Chinese space experts warned on Thursday that hyping a space race with China could backfire, fueling unrealistic deadlines, greater cost overruns and scientific risks, while failing to address NASA's underlying engineering and management challenges. They also stressed that China's Tianwen-3 mission follows its own scientific roadmap rather than seeking to outpace the US. US space news site Space.com reported on US local time Wednesday that NASA is launching a fresh effort to reassess how samples collected by its Perseverance rover could be brought back to Earth, following years of mounting costs, technical difficulties and uncertainty surrounding the Mars Sample Return (MSR) program. Notably, the report identified China's progress on its Tianwen-3 Mars sample-return mission as a "forcing factor" prompting NASA to reconsider its approach. Pang Zhihao, a senior space expert, told the Global Times on Thursday that placing the two Mars sample-return missions within a competitive framework reflects a familiar narrative in US media rather than the fundamental nature of space exploration. "The Chinese and US Mars sample-return missions are independently planned scientific projects, with different schedules and technical approaches. Tianwen-3 is rooted in China's step-by-step planetary exploration program, with the goal of obtaining Martian samples for cutting-edge scientific research, rather than benchmarking itself against or catching up with the US," Pang said. Kang Guohua, a senior member of the Chinese Society of Astronautics, told the Global Times that hyping the so-called "China pressure" serves to divert attention from NASA's own cost overruns and management failures, turning China into an external target to justify funding demands. China's Tianwen-3 mission is seeking evidence of whether life has ever existed on Mars, the mission's chief scientist, Hou Zengqian, told Xinhua in September. The mission aims to bring Martian samples back to Earth for detailed analysis. As a key step in China's planetary exploration program, Tianwen-3, planned for launch around 2028, is expected to become the first Mars sample-return mission in human history. NASA's Perseverance rover has collected samples on Mars. A follow-up mission would be needed to bring them to Earth. In contrast, Tianwen-3 aims to accomplish both sampling and return in a single mission, Xinhua reported then. Pang explained that the mission's schedule is determined by objective scientific and engineering constraints, including Earth-Mars launch opportunities occurring approximately every 26 months, launch capacity, liftoff from the Martian surface, orbital rendezvous, sample containment and planetary protection. "Hastily pursuing the 'first' in deep-space exploration could compress essential testing and verification procedures, creating serious risks," Pang warned. NASA's Mars Sample Return program has faced repeated difficulties over its technical complexity, escalating costs and prolonged development schedule. Previous assessments suggested the program could cost as much as $11 billion, with the return of samples potentially delayed until 2040, according to the Space.com report. Pang said NASA's difficulties stem from a combination of complex engineering requirements, cost overruns and project management challenges, rather than any single technological obstacle. He argued that repeated changes to mission designs, shifting requirements and complicated supply-chain coordination have further increased costs and slowed progress. "Portraying China as a competitor through a geopolitical rivalry narrative may help secure congressional funding in the short term, but it cannot fundamentally resolve engineering challenges," Pang told the Global Times. "Geopolitical competition narratives cannot solve engineering problems. Simply warning that China might get there first will not make billions of dollars in cost overruns disappear," said Kang, who is also a professor of aerospace engineering at Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics. "China's Tianwen-3 is proceeding at its own pace, targeting a launch in 2028 and a sample return in 2031, with a streamlined mission architecture and an emphasis on risk control. Successfully bringing Martian samples back to Earth matters far more than winning a race to be first." Kang argued that the real obstacles facing the US program lie in project management and resource allocation, rather than the speed of China's progress. "Ironically, such rhetoric amounts to an acknowledgment that China's space program has become a timeline benchmark that the US can no longer ignore when planning its own missions," he said. Pang warned that politically driven competition could encourage unrealistic deadlines, potentially forcing projects to accelerate development before critical technologies have been adequately verified, further aggravating budget overruns and technical risks. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun remarked on April 24, China's Space Day, that space is not an arena for rivalry among major powers and that China would continue to pursue open cooperation in space exploration.

item.title: Xi calls for carrying forward Sun Yat-sen's legacy in national rejuvenation drive
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12 12:27:00
Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, addresses a gathering to commemorate the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 12, 2026. (Xinhua/Yue Yuewei) Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday called for carrying forward the legacy of Sun Yat-sen, one of the nation's revered revolutionary forefathers, to make joint efforts for national rejuvenation and turn into reality the great dream of all Chinese people since the advent of modern times. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks at a gathering held in Beijing to commemorate the 160th anniversary of Sun's birth. Born in 1866, Sun led the Revolution of 1911 more than a century ago to abolish the absolute monarchy that had ruled China for thousands of years. Sun died in 1925. Thursday's gathering in the Great Hall of the People was attended by about 3,000 people, including senior Chinese leaders Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi, who are members of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee. Wang presided over the event. Xi met with Sun's relatives and representatives of overseas guests before the event started. In his speech, Xi hailed Sun as a great national hero, a great patriot and a great pioneer of China's democratic revolution. He said that Chinese communists are the most steadfast supporters, loyal collaborators, and faithful successors to the revolutionary cause initiated by Sun. For more than 100 years, the CPC has led the Chinese people in writing the most magnificent chapter in the history of the Chinese nation, Xi said. "The best way for us to remember Dr. Sun is to emulate, inherit and carry forward his invaluable spirit, steadily advancing our endeavors to build a great country and rejuvenate our nation," Xi said. Highlighting Sun's lifelong devotion to the country, Xi called on all Chinese people to learn from Sun and promote patriotism to strive for a strong and prosperous China. He also lauded Sun's dedication to the people, underscoring the imperative of always putting the people first and serving them wholeheartedly. On the new journey, it is essential to make solid headway in promoting well-rounded personal development and common prosperity for all, Xi stressed. Noting that Sun devoted his life to the pursuit of truth, Xi stressed the need to learn from Sun's example, advance theoretical exploration and innovation with courage, and continue to write new chapters in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of the times. Xi called on the Chinese people to carry forward Sun's unyielding determination, rise to challenges ahead and break new ground in the country's development. "We must carry forward the fighting spirit, build up our ability, be ready to withstand high winds, choppy waters, and even dangerous storms, and overcome all the risks and challenges we face on the way forward," Xi said. Calling on people to learn from Sun's commitment to unity, Xi also emphasized adhering to the united front and strengthening the great unity among all the sons and daughters of the Chinese nation. Highlighting Sun's global vision, Xi called for vigorously promoting the common values of humanity and actively advancing the building of a community with a shared future for humanity. "Dr. Sun always upheld national unity and ethnic solidarity, and resolutely opposed any word or act attempting to split the country and divide the nation," Xi said. Resolving the Taiwan question and realizing the complete reunification of the motherland is an unwavering historical mission for the CPC, the shared aspiration of all Chinese people, and a natural requirement for the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, Xi stressed. People on both sides of the Taiwan Strait and all Chinese at home and abroad should join hands to oppose the "Taiwan independence" secessionist forces, and work together for the peaceful development of cross-Strait relations and the complete reunification of the motherland, Xi said. "On the basis of adhering to the one-China principle and the 1992 Consensus, we are willing to engage in dialogue and consultations with people of vision and insight from all sectors in Taiwan on matters related to cross-Strait relations and national reunification," Xi said. "We will definitely give full consideration to Taiwan's realities and take full account of the interests and feelings of our compatriots in Taiwan," Xi said. "But we will never leave any room for 'Taiwan independence' separatist activities in any form." "The historical trends are unstoppable. The complete reunification of our motherland must be realized, and it can, without doubt, be realized," Xi said. A gathering commemorating the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth is held at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 12, 2026. Xi Jinping, Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi attended the gathering here on Thursday. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, addresses a gathering to commemorate the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 12, 2026. (Xinhua/Yao Dawei)

item.title: China's Mazu early weather warning box makes global debut
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12 11:14:00
China intelligent meteorological solution MAZU is seen on display during the 2026 World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai. Photo: VCG China's Mazu all-in-one box, an intelligent meteorological early warning solution, was officially launched globally at the COP31 High-Level Forum on South-South Cooperation on Climate Change in Antalya, Turkey, the China Meteorological Administration (CMA) said in a WeChat post on Thursday. MAZU, short for multi-hazard, alert, zero-gap and universal, is an AI-driven meteorological early warning platform named after the Chinese guardian goddess of the sea. The box is a lightweight, integrated hardware-software early warning solution designed to run the Mazu platform locally. It integrates storage, intelligent computing, networking, display and computation. Compatible with Ethernet, 5G and satellite communications, it delivers capabilities including nowcasting, an overview dashboard, operational monitoring and on-site AI assistance, enabling developing countries to rapidly ingest local observational data, according to the release. The box can run operations independently on site or connect to cloud resources and integrate with existing operational systems for coordinated operations. It supports modular expansion and continuous upgrading, helping local agencies strengthen their early warning operational capabilities, said the release. Given wide climatic variations worldwide, the CMA has worked closely with national meteorological and hydrological agencies to adapt Mazu into a weather tool tuned to local conditions. On November 1, China officially delivered a Mazu all-in-one box to Sri Lanka, which is expected to enter operational service by the end of 2026. It features custom-built modules for aviation, maritime and other sectors, aiming to help the Southern Asian country shore up its multi-hazard meteorological early-warning capabilities, CMA said. China delivered a customized version of its homegrown AI-powered meteorological early warning system to Nepal on September 22 to help the country improve early warning and disaster response. The move came after the CMA gave Nepal's meteorological department a version of Mazu for cloud-based trial use on August 29, following a deadly mudslide at the Gyirong-Rasuwa border crossing on the China-Nepal border, the Xinhua News Agency reported. As of October 2026, the Mazu solution had been deployed in eight countries, including Pakistan, Ethiopia and Sri Lanka, and tested through cloud-based trials in more than 50 countries, according to CMA. Global Times

item.title: Teodoro has become an isolated figure in Manila
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12 09:45:00
Philippines Secretary of National Defense Gilberto Teodoro Jr. delivers his speech during a plenary session of the International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS) Shangri-la Dialogue Defense Summit in Singapore, 31 May 2026. Photo: VCG Following a public statement by the Philippine Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) criticizing the inappropriate China-related remarks of "certain government officials" for damaging the country's international credibility, Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has also weighed in. On November 10, Marcos, through his spokesperson, called on officials to exercise "caution" when making public remarks concerning China and to consider the potential diplomatic repercussions of their statements. This marks the highest-level response so far from the Philippine government to anti-China politicians at home. Although no names were mentioned, everyone knows who the message was directed at. The target was none other than Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro. Marcos' statement elevated the DFA's criticism into an explicit restraint imposed at the presidential level. The clarity of this signal exceeded many people's expectations. After being criticized by the DFA, Teodoro had defiantly declared that he "will listen only to the President of the Republic of the Philippines." Now, however, that protective shield has been unceremoniously stripped away. If Teodoro continues his anti-China theatrics, he will effectively be challenging Marcos himself, forcing the president either to admit that he cannot control his defense secretary or to take more decisive personnel or policy measures. Since Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi spoke by phone with Philippine Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro and criticized a handful of Philippine politicians as "irrational and intolerable," calls within the Philippines to hold Teodoro accountable have grown increasingly vocal. On November 9, The Manila Times published an article titled "Teodoro should go," arguing that the defense secretary is a huge liability for the government and is "worsening Marcos' image as a president who can't even control his officials." Philippine public opinion had previously speculated that Teodoro dared to behave so arrogantly because he enjoyed the president's indulgence or even tacit approval. However, Marcos' emphasis on the "diplomatic repercussions" of officials' remarks demonstrates that the country's top leadership has come to recognize that allowing Teodoro and others to carry on unchecked has raised questions both at home and abroad about who actually speaks for Manila. The Philippines' two-track approach to China policy should indeed come to an end. What Manila needs is not a competition over who can appear tougher on China, but a pragmatic framework capable of managing differences while advancing cooperation, thereby avoiding the recurring pattern of putting out fires only to see them deliberately reignited. Continued indulgence will merely allow personalized anti-China narratives, such as those promoted by Teodoro, to further erode the country's credibility. Ultimately, those who suffer are ordinary Filipinos, whose livelihoods depend on a stable external environment and predictable market conditions. As for Teodoro, he has only himself to blame for becoming an isolated figure. It is also worth noting that his hard-line approach has been encouraged by external forces. This means that for Manila to put its China policy in order, it must do more than rein in a single cabinet minister. It must also recalibrate the relationship between its security and diplomatic priorities, clearly distinguishing between its own core national interests and the agendas of others.

item.title: PLA's 'silent drills' around Taiwan region? There is little to speculate about: Global Times editorial
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11 23:59:00
Illustration: Chen Xia/GT Rather than obsessively scrutinizing situation maps and speculating about every movement, the DPP authorities should recognize an indisputable fact: In the fight against separatism and for national reunification, the PLA will never be absent and will never hesitate to act. Any separatist attempt to seek "Taiwan independence" by relying on external forces or military means will face severe punishment and is doomed to fail. Recently, a map dotted with red markers has become a hot topic on the island of Taiwan. It began when diehard "Taiwan independence" separatist Joseph Wu posted the map on social media, claiming that the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) Navy and China Coast Guard (CCG) had "deployed 100+ vessels in the western Pacific." Two US think tanks jointly released a report, using a string of "may be" to speculate that the PLA was conducting a "major, unannounced military exercise." Taiwan region's so-called defense minister then followed suit, distorting the nature of these activities and smearing the PLA's normal maritime operations as "undermining" regional "peace and stability." Various forces have played along, taking turns speculating about and hyping the purported "silent drills," their objectives and details. The whole episode reeks of a calculated political effort to deliberately stoke tensions. There is little mystery here that warrants such excessive speculation. Whether it is the series of military exercises including "Joint Sword" and "Strait Thunder," or regular naval patrols, and law-based maritime law enforcement patrols by the CCG, they are all legitimate arrangements within China's sovereignty - lawful, reasonable, and beyond dispute. Take the PLA Navy's Liaoning aircraft carrier group training in the western Pacific, for example. China's Ministry of National Defense has publicly stated that the training was part of the PLA's annual routine schedule, was not directed at any specific country or target, and was consistent with international law and practice. Not to mention that the decision on whether to conduct military exercises, when to hold them and whether to release relevant information rests entirely with the PLA. Such decisions are made independently in accordance with China's defense needs and the situation across the Taiwan Straits, without any obligation to report to or seek approval from any other party. By deliberately portraying legitimate activities that have been clearly identified by official statements and are part of routine training arrangements as a "mysterious, unannounced military exercise," and repeatedly speculating about and sensationalizing this fabricated concept, certain forces are essentially trying to stoke public anxiety. In addition, years of exercises conducted under explicit code names and announced in coordinated public releases have made the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities accustomed to a familiar playbook for managing public opinion on the island. Military activities around the Taiwan Straits are now shifting from periodic, concentrated operations to an around-the-clock, regularized presence. As early as April 2025, when the PLA Eastern Theater Command conducted joint exercises without an official code name, experts pointed out that such drills "have become routine and are nothing out of the ordinary for the PLA." Those with a guilty conscience can be startled by even the sound of ordinary footsteps. The Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities' alarmist reaction to the "red-dot map" exposes their helplessness in the face of the new normal across the Taiwan Straits. They can neither deny the sovereign legitimacy of the People's Liberation Army's (PLA) operations nor rely on their old tactics to cope with a military presence that has defied their expectations. All they can do is turn a single map into a political spectacle, manufacture panic out of "silence," and falsely label the PLA's legitimate operations as "undermining peace and stability." For the majority of Taiwan compatriots, however, the PLA's regular presence around the Taiwan Straits serves to constrain the room for reckless moves by "Taiwan independence" separatist forces through sustained, visible and predictable deterrence, reducing the likelihood of miscalculation and dangerous adventurism. The stronger the deterrent capability of the people's armed forces, the more solid the guarantee that Taiwan residents can stay away from the ravages of war and enjoy peaceful, stable lives. This is a truth that cannot be turned on its head by a few slogans about "undermining peace and stability." The DPP authorities have repeatedly hyped the so-called "silent military drills," hoping to prolong their political survival by stoking tensions. Yet such tactics cannot stop the balance of power across the Straits from continuing to shift in a direction favorable to national reunification. If the "Taiwan independence" separatist forces were truly as confident as they claim, why would they be so unnerved by routine naval activities at sea? Their anxiety reveals that they are acutely aware of their predicament in going against the tide of history and deeply fearful of the balance of strength across the Straits and the direction of public sentiment. What they fear is not any particular military exercise or drill, but an overarching trend that is beyond their control. Let us put it more plainly: The PLA's regular presence around the Taiwan Straits will not change because of the political hype surrounding a "red-dot map," nor will it be halted by a chorus of accusations about "undermining peace and stability." Rather than obsessively scrutinizing situation maps and speculating about every movement, the DPP authorities should recognize an indisputable fact: In the fight against separatism and for national reunification, the PLA will never be absent and will never hesitate to act. Any separatist attempt to seek "Taiwan independence" by relying on external forces or military means will face severe punishment and is doomed to fail. National reunification is the ultimate outcome that leaves no room for speculation.

item.title: GT Voice: What Washington risks by tightening tech curbs on China?
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11 22:26:00
The photo taken from atop the Washington Monument on Nov. 17, 2025 shows the construction site where the East Wing of the White House was recently demolished, while construction crews prepare the area for the White House's new ballroom, in Washington, D.C., the United States. (Xinhua/Hu Yousong) Reuters reported on Tuesday, citing three people familiar with the matter, that Microsoft, other companies and trade groups have pressed Washington to halt plans to bar imports from China of new models of optical transceivers, a key component in artificial intelligence (AI) data centers. This little-noticed component is emerging as an unexpected test for the AI industry in the US. These discussions are taking place against a sensitive backdrop. Some are seizing on the controversy surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to stir unfounded fears and suspicion about Chinese technology, apparently seeking to build momentum for another round of restrictions on China's tech sector. Viewing technology through an ever-expanding national security lens could ultimately undermine the AI development the US is seeking to accelerate. Optical transceivers may seem like a minor, separate issue, largely unrelated to the current debate. Yet the episode is telling a sign of what is at stake. Whenever US-China technology supply chains face the prospect of disruption, US tech companies are often among the first to feel the pressure. Why are Microsoft and other US companies so alarmed by reports that Washington may restrict these imports? The answer lies in the structure of the global supply chains. Chinese manufacturers occupy a substantial position in the global optical transceiver market. According to Counterpoint Research, Chinese optical module manufacturers account for nearly two-thirds of global unit supply and approximately 60 percent of global optical datacom transceiver revenue. Can the US afford to build its data centers without Chinese optical transceivers? These components enable data to travel at the speed of light over fiber-optic cables, making them essential to data center operations. John Miller, an executive vice president of policy and general counsel of the Information Technology Industry Council, told Reuters that such a ban "really threatens to arguably grind" data center rollouts to a halt. This exposes a fundamental contradiction. The US is seeking to contain China's technological development through tighter restrictions and, in some areas, supply chain "decoupling." Yet it also wants to accelerate its own technological progress, which increasingly relies on Chinese-sourced materials and components, as well as access to the Chinese market. These two goals are increasingly at odds. As China's technological capabilities advance, Chinese companies are gaining a stronger foothold in the supply chains for components and critical technologies. At the same time, the expansion of the Chinese market is creating opportunities for US companies. The technology industries of the two countries remain deeply intertwined, reflecting substantial scope for mutual benefits. The more China advances technologically, the sharper the contradiction facing Washington becomes, and its efforts to contain China are increasingly at odds with its own need for technological development. The optical transceiver issue shows how acute this contradiction has already become. As Miller warned, a ban on Chinese suppliers could bring US data center rollouts to a halt. Washington may therefore be nearing the point at which further restrictions would directly obstruct its own AI development. That is why Microsoft and other US companies are so alarmed. Yet the growing tendency in US public discourse to hype the so-called China threat and broaden the scope of national security concerns risks further disrupting supply chains from which the US tech industry itself stands to benefit from. If that happens, AI development in the US will be among the first to pay the price. The US should think twice. The optical transceiver should serve as a wake-up call, showing that there are limits to how far Washington can go in restricting Chinese technology before those restrictions begin to undermine its own interests. In the wake of the midterm elections, US data center development is facing mounting headwinds at home. Tightening restrictions on Chinese technology would only compound these obstacles. Efforts to curb China's technological progress may end up holding back US' own AI development.

item.title: China updates standards for key robot component amid rising demand
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11 21:06:00
Visitors observe a humanoid robot on display at the Shanghai International Intelligent Home Expo in Shanghai on September 28, 2026. Photo: VCG China has revised two national standards governing harmonic drive reducers, a key transmission component used in industrial and humanoid robots, in a move aimed at improving product quality and supporting the development of its domestic precision machinery industry, the Guangming Daily reported. The standards, GB/T 12601-2026, covering basic terminology for harmonic gear drives, and GB/T 14118-2026, covering harmonic drive reducers, were highlighted at a technical seminar and standards launch conference held recently in Shengzhou, East China's Zhejiang Province. The revisions mark the first major updates to the two standards in more than three decades, the report noted. They are scheduled to take effect on April 1, 2027, according to China's National Standard Information Public Service Platform. Harmonic drive reducers are precision transmission devices installed in robot joints. They use controlled elastic deformation of a flexible gear to transmit motion and torque, allowing robots to achieve precise movements in a compact space. They are widely used in industrial robots, collaborative robots and humanoid robots. Their importance is expected to grow as humanoid robots develop. According to industry estimates, a single humanoid robot may require multiple harmonic reducers across its joints, making the component an important part of the industry's supply chain. China's harmonic reducer market was valued at approximately 3.8 billion yuan ($570 million) in 2025 and is expected to reach 4.8 billion yuan in 2026, according to estimates by industry research firm Zhiyan Consulting. Demand in the robotics sector is also projected to expand rapidly. Shipments of harmonic reducers for robots in China are expected to increase from 1.4 million units in 2025 to 20.7 million units by 2030, representing a compound annual growth rate of 72.4 percent, according to estimates by China Insights Consultancy. The expansion, however, comes with mounting competitive pressure on domestic manufacturers. For years, Japan's Harmonic Drive Systems and other overseas suppliers held a strong position in the high-end market. Chinese manufacturers have gradually expanded their presence through research and development, improvements in manufacturing processes and efforts to replace imported products. The progress has been significant, but competition is increasingly shifting from securing market share to improving product performance, reliability and cost efficiency. Against this backdrop, the two revised standards are expected to help address some of these challenges. The first, GB/T 12601-2026, establishes a unified set of terms used across the industry, helping researchers, manufacturers and testing institutions communicate and work with consistent definitions. The second, GB/T 14118-2026, sets out requirements for harmonic drive reducers, including product categories, quality requirements and testing procedures. In practical terms, it provides manufacturers and customers with a common benchmark for judging whether products meet the required standards. The revision also comes as China's broader robotics industry seeks to strengthen its domestic supply chain. In 2023, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology issued guidelines for the development of humanoid robots, identifying core components, including precision transmission systems, as important areas for technological progress.
